text: dsh-doctor 是面向 DSH profile 的配置诊断插件，可作为命令行工具使用，也能在 DSH 中注册 config_doctor 工具，让 agent 检查当前 profile。它比较实际配置树与默认配置树，发现 patch 整块替换配置后丢失的字段、指向不存在条目的 patch、工具名称冲突、未挂载或长期未发布的第三方插件，并报告条目增删和启用状态。命令行还可查看配置树概况、输出 JSON、离线跳过 npm 查询，或补回部分丢失字段。适合排查设置未生效和升级前检查；需要 Node.js 18+ 与可用的 dsh。

dsh-doctor checks DSH profiles as a CLI or agent tool. It compares the composed tree with defaults to find dropped config fields, invalid patch targets, tool name collisions, and plugin mounting issues. The CLI can explain the tree or restore some dropped fields. Requires Node.js 18+ and dsh.
帮我找出 DSH 配置里写了却没有生效的 patch。
检查改配置时是不是把原有字段意外删掉了。
我想看看 profile 里装了哪些组件，哪些处于关闭状态。
检查我装的插件有没有被 profile 实际加载。
想知道两个插件是否注册了同名工具，导致启动冲突。
升级 DSH 之前，怎么确认自己的配置改动仍然有效？
Why is a patch targeting an entry that no longer exists being ignored?
Show me which settings disappeared after I changed a profile config block.
Can I inspect the active and disabled entries in my DSH profile?
dsh-doctor 的功能「检查 patch 丢失配置」：比较组合后的配置与默认树，指出 patch 替换整个 config 后缺失的默认字段，并给出可恢复的字段和值。通过 CLI 检查 profile 时自动运行。
dsh-doctor 的功能「配置树与问题概览」：检查不存在的 patch 目标、重复工具名、未挂载或长期未发布的插件及条目开关状态。运行默认检查流程时输出问题，使用 --explain 可改为展示条目数量和启停概况。
dsh-doctor 的功能「agent 配置诊断工具」：安装为 DSH 插件后注册 config_doctor 工具。agent 可指定 profile，工具返回条目数和精简的问题清单，供对话中解释当前配置问题。
dsh-doctor 的功能「补回丢失字段」：CLI 使用 --fix 时，将能确定的默认字段和值补进对应 patch 的 config 区块，并在旁边保留 .bak 备份；嵌套路径等无法安全插入的项目会列出供手动处理。

dsh-doctor README · dsh-doctor：[](https://github.com/asdf17128/dsh-doctor/actions/workflows/ci.yml) **Your dsh config has settings that silently stopped applying. This tells you which ones.** English | [中文](README.zh.md) ```sh npx github:asdf17128/dsh-doctor ``` One command, ten seconds, read-only. No config, no signup, no dependencies. ---

dsh-doctor README · Why your setting isn't taking effect：Two dsh behaviours boot cleanly with exit code 0, so nothing tells you:

**A patch replaces an entry's whole `config`.** You change one field; every
sibling field you did not restate disappears from the tree that boots. The
plugin then runs on defaults you never chose.

```diff
  config:
    fallbackMaxWords: 12
-   fallbackMaxBytes: 40      ← gone, silently
-   maxTitleBytes: 80         ← gone, silently
section: Why your setting isn't taking effect

dsh-doctor README · Why your setting isn't taking effect：**A typo in an entry id is inert.** Write `agent-defualt-model` and dsh prints
one stderr line, then boots without your change. Launching the Web UI, you never
see it — you just wonder why nothing happened.

Both get worse after an upgrade renames an entry id, and neither surfaces until
behaviour drifts weeks later.
section: Why your setting isn't taking effect

text:
dsh-doctor README · What it looks like：```
dsh-doctor · profile web · 130 entries (25 disabled)

✗ patch on "session-title" dropped 2 default config fields  config-clobber
    @deepseek-ai/dsh-session-title

dsh-doctor README · As a dsh plugin：Installed into a profile, dsh-doctor registers a `config_doctor` tool so the
agent can inspect the configuration it is itself running under:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-doctor
```

Then ask it — "why isn't my session-title setting taking effect?" — and it
answers from the composed tree instead of guessing. Read-only; `--fix` stays
CLI-only, because rewriting your patch file is not something an agent should do
from a chat turn.

dsh-doctor README · Checks：| Rule | Severity | What it catches |
|---|---|---|
| `config-clobber` | error | Default config fields your patch dropped by not restating them |
| `dead-patch` | error | A patch targeting an entry id that is not in the tree (with a did-you-mean) |
| `tool-collision` | error | Two mounted plugins registering the same tool name — dsh refuses to start |
| `plugin-not-mounted` | warn | A plugin installed into the profile that nothing ever loads |
| `plugin-stale` | warn | A third-party plugin with no npm release in 180+ days |
| `entry-removed` | warn | A shipped entry your patch layer removed |
| `entry-toggled` / `entry-added` | info | Every other difference from the shipped profile, so the diff is visible |

dsh-doctor README · Explain mode：A healthy install gets "no problems found", which tells you nothing about what
you are running. `--explain` answers that instead:

```
Your harness: 130 entries, 103 active, 25 disabled, 2 conditional

Web UI                  32
  Tools                   18  (16 off)

Entries whose `disabled:` is a `!!js` expression are reported as *conditional*
rather than collapsed to a boolean — the answer depends on the machine that
boots, and the tool never evaluates your config to find out.

dsh-doctor README · Usage：```sh
npx dsh-doctor                      # check the web profile
npx dsh-doctor --explain            # describe the tree instead of checking it
npx dsh-doctor --profile headless   # another profile
npx dsh-doctor --verbose            # include informational notes

Exit codes: `0` clean or warnings only · `1` at least one error · `2` could not inspect.

Useful in CI, or as a pre-upgrade check:

```sh
npx dsh-doctor --quiet || echo "review your patches before upgrading dsh"
```

dsh-doctor README · `--fix`：`--fix` restates the fields a patch dropped, writing them back into the same
`config:` block with the values the shipped profile declared:

```diff
  - id: session-title
    config:
      fallbackMaxWords: 12
+     fallbackMaxBytes: 40

dsh-doctor README · `--fix`：It edits inside that block only — comments, ordering and every other entry stay
byte-identical — and writes a `.bak` beside the file first. A nested key path is
reported for you to restate by hand rather than guessed at, and `dead-patch`
findings are never auto-fixed because renaming versus deleting is your call.

dsh-doctor README · How it works：It shells out to dsh's own composition: - `dsh --profile

--dump-config` — the tree that actually boots (bundles → profile patch → home patch → overlays) - `dsh --profile

--dump-default-config` — the same tree without your user layer Every finding is a diff between those two, so the report can attribute a change to *your* patches rather than to an upstream default. It also reads the profile's `package.json` and `cordis.patch.yml` files.

dsh-doctor README · How it works：It never boots a plugin and never evaluates the `!!js` expressions in your config.

Two caveats about writes, since "read-only" is easy to overstate:

dsh-doctor README · How it works：- `--fix` writes, by design — into the flagged `config:` block only, `.bak` first.
- Composing a profile is dsh's own operation, and dsh materialises a template
  the first time a profile is used. So running this against a `$DSH_HOME` that
  has no profiles yet will leave `profiles/<name>/` behind — created by dsh, not
  by us, but worth knowing before you point it at a pristine home.

dsh-doctor README · Install and uninstall：As a CLI, nothing to install — `npx dsh-doctor` runs it.

As a plugin:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:asdf17128/dsh-doctor   # install
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-doctor                 # uninstall
```

Removing it drops the `config_doctor` tool and leaves nothing behind: the plugin
never writes to your Harness home.

dsh-doctor README · Compatibility：Verified against `@deepseek-ai/dsh` **0.1.0-rc.5**. dsh is in developer preview
and ships breaking changes; the checks read `--dump-config` output, so a change
to that format is what would break them first. Open an issue if a newer dsh
reports something odd and I will pin down the difference.
dsh-doctor README · Requirements：Node 18+ and a working `dsh` (local `node_modules/.bin/dsh` is preferred, otherwise one on `PATH`).

dsh-doctor README · Why this exists：dsh is in developer preview and ships breaking changes; its "everything is a plugin" model means your tree is a stack of patch layers, and the layering rules are unforgiving in exactly one direction — the failure modes above are silent. This tool is the thing that tells you.

Behaviour verified against `@deepseek-ai/dsh` 0.1.0-rc.5.
dsh-doctor README · Contributing：Issues and PRs welcome — especially new check rules with a reproduction. Run the tests with `npm test`.
